materials.title: Part 1: food and cooking
materials.instructions: The examiner asks you some questions about yourself. Answer each question in two to four sentences.
speakingQuestions: What kind of food do you like to eat?
Do you often cook at home?
Is there any food you disliked as a child but enjoy now?
What is a traditional dish from your country?
Do you prefer eating at home or in restaurants?

materials.title: Part 1: phones and technology
materials.instructions: The examiner asks you some questions about yourself. Answer each question in two to four sentences.
speakingQuestions: How often do you use your phone each day?
What do you mainly use your phone for?
Have you ever tried to spend a day without your phone?
Do you prefer texting or calling people? Why?
Would you like to have a newer phone?

materials.title: Part 2: a teacher who influenced you
materials.instructions: You will have one minute to prepare. You can make notes. Then talk for one to two minutes.
materials.prompt: Describe a teacher who had a strong influence on you.
bullets: and explain how they influenced you
materials.scoringGuidance: A good long turn uses past tenses accurately, gives specific anecdotes (one memorable lesson or comment) and ends with reflection on the lasting effect, rather than listing adjectives.

materials.title: Part 2: a useful piece of technology
materials.instructions: You will have one minute to prepare. You can make notes. Then talk for one to two minutes.
materials.prompt: Describe a piece of technology (not a phone) that you find useful.
bullets: and explain why it is useful to you

materials.title: Part 3: teachers and learning
materials.instructions: The examiner asks you more general questions linked to the Part 2 topic. Give developed answers with reasons and examples.
speakingQuestions: What qualities make someone a good teacher?
Do you think teachers are more or less respected than they were in the past?
Could online lessons ever completely replace classroom teachers?
Should teachers be paid according to their students' exam results?

materials.title: Part 3: technology in daily life
materials.instructions: The examiner asks you more general questions linked to the Part 2 topic. Give developed answers with reasons and examples.
speakingQuestions: How has technology changed the way families spend time together?
Do older people find it harder to adapt to new technology? Why?
Is it possible to depend too much on technology?
What kinds of technology do you think will be common in homes in twenty years?
